accuracy.evidence: Every fact recomputed: 9 × 7 = 70 − 7 = 63, 11 × 11 = 121, 11 × 12 = 120 + 12 = 132, 12 × 7 = 70 + 14 = 84, 132 ÷ 12 = 11, 56 ÷ 7 = 8, 7 × 8 = 56. The count of squares left after shading 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 was checked by enumerating the grid: 16 squares, 10 distinct facts (listed in the adult text and m6), and 78 distinct facts in the whole square. NC Year 4 statement and the Multiplication Tables Check format (June, 25 questions, 6 seconds each) checked against DfE/STA documents.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented derived-fact slips: taking away 1 instead of one group for the 9s (prediction '1', 'Take away just 1' button, m1, tag one), adding 2 instead of two groups for the 12s (prediction '2', 'Just add 2' button, m2, tag two), stretching the 11s digit pattern (prediction '1212', 'Write 1212' button, p3, tag join), subtracting once for division ('Take 12 away' button, m8, tag sub), adding instead of multiplying (m5, tag add), near facts (tag near) and turnarounds counted as new facts (p5, tag turn).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtt12 works on the whole 12 × 12 square and the 7, 9, 11 and 12 tables: tapping table headers to shade rows and columns until 16 squares remain, dragging a cover line down the tenth column of a 7 × 10 dot array, dragging a 1 × n strip onto a 10 × n block, sliding a split line through a 12 × 7 array, and hopping on 12s and 7s stepping stones for division. flagttfam (2, 5, 10, fact families), flagttdbl (doubling to 3, 4, 8) and flagsixes (counting in 6s) do none of these.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner sees the result before it is named: the 'squares still new' counter falls to 16 and the 16 products appear; the headline updates 70 − 1, 70 − 2 … 70 − 7 as each row's tenth dot is covered; joining the strip shows 120 + 12; the split readout changes for every position and turns green at 10 + 2; each hop reveals k × 12 until 132 appears at the 11th stone. Step text then states the rule.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions with a tempting wrong option: 'about 100' squares still new, 9 × 7 is 10 × 7 take away '1', 11 × 12 = '1212' or '122', 12 × 7 is 10 × 7 plus '2', and 132 ÷ 12 = '120'. Each is disproved by the task, and the reveal line names the correct option.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eight rotating questions (9 × 6, 12 × 6, 11 × 12, 132 ÷ 11, 7 × 8, the 8 × 7 turnaround, 9 × 12, 84 ÷ 7). Wrong options carry tags one, two, join, sub, add, near and turn; each message names the slip, e.g. 'Twelve lots is ten lots and two LOTS: 12 × 6 = 60 + 12, not 60 + 2.'

readability.evidence: Kid text FK grade -1.6 and adult 7.4 (family targets 5.0 and 10.0): short sentences built around worked numbers. Maths vocabulary from the Year 4 programme (multiple, product, factor, commutative, inverse, derived fact) is in the adult text; the kid text uses 'lots' and 'turnaround' with examples.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs: only 10 new facts, the 9s, the 11s and 12s, division facts. Adult: NC and MTC context with key words, the commutativity count and distributive strategies, seven named mistakes, the lab steps. No filler pattern matched and the overlap gate passed against lessons 640 and 641.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android dark and iPhone 13 light screenshots after Show me for every step: the 13 × 13 square fits with 10 px labels and visible products; the 7 × 10 dots and cover line fit; the 11s block was shortened (row height 3.3% of the canvas) after the strip started too close to it and its label clashed with the hint; the 12 × 7 array and knob fit; the stepping stones sit in a 4 × 3 grid. The Show me for the hops step was sped up to 150 ms per hop so it finishes inside the walk timeout.

accessibility.evidence: Button twins for every drag or tap: 'Shade the <n>s' for each known table plus 'Shade the 7s' (which explains why not), 'Cover one more row' / 'Take away just 1', 'Join 1 × n to 10 × n' / 'Write 1212', 'Split line left/right' / 'Just add 2', 'Hop to k × n' / 'Take n away'. Canvas aria-label and the live region carry each message. walk.cjs passed axe WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
